story: Riding high in Germany on the world's oldest suspended railway
text: Here is a wonderful video, riding the Wuppertal Schwebebahn in 1902 and 2015 side by side: [VIDEO] As noted in the description, the 1902 video plays in real time, and the 2015 video has some cuts and framerate adjustments to keep them in sync.

story: Ride through Wuppertal on ‘the flying train’ in clear footage from 1902
text: A side-by-side view of 1902 vs current: [VIDEO] As an aside, I find it interesting that this steel wasn't reclaimed sometime during WWII when the industrial machine was desperate for iron/metal.

story: Wuppertal's suspended monorail proved its doubters wrong [video]
text: There is a semi-famous video from 1902 recording a ride on the then new Schwebebahn. MoMa digitised it and someone on Youtube did a side-by-side-recording of 1902 vs. 2015: [VIDEO] There are two other suspended monorails in the Ruhr are, both driver-less and shorter, built in the 80s and 90s by Siemens, the H-Bahn at Dortmund University and the Skytrain at Düsseldorf Airport. I drove the H-Bahn daily, because computer science back then was distributed all about the campus. Still have fond memories about it. (Less so about the degree.) The Tim Traveller on Youtube recently did a video about it: [LINK]
